newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sets 30 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sets 30 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.

text.p: The Central Bank of Venezuela announced for Wednesday morning a 20 billion bolivar ($41 million) auction of 177-day VE6MTMA=RR "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills with a 17.80 percent coupon.

The bank said it would also offer five billion bolivars ($10 million) in 266-day bills VE9MTMA=RR with a 18.19 percent coupon, and another five billion bolivars of 358-day bills VE1YTMA=RR with a 18.60 percent coupon.
Some 25 billion bolivars of TEMs are due to mature on Thursday.

Coupons at the Wednesday auction are marginally up from last week's 100 billion bolivar issue. Then 177-, 266- and 358- day notes carried 17.48, 17.85, and 18.24 percent coupons respectively for effective yields of 17.80, 19.93 and 21.13 percent.
Despite the small auction, yields are expected to rise on a liquidity squeeze in Venezuelan financial markets that sent the overnight interbank lending rate shooting up to 90 percent on Monday.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
